title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is a 54-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding their T2DM. The patient reports being adherent to their current medication regimen. They report stable energy levels and no acute concerns since the last visit. The patient currently manages their condition with a combination of long-term insulin and an oral hypoglycemic agent. They report no new symptoms or issues with their current treatment plan.

Medication List
- Insulin
- Metformin

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no visible skin changes or lesions. Neurological exam is unremarkable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications.

Plan
1. Continue current regimen of insulin and metformin.
2. Patient instructed to continue monitoring blood glucose levels at home.
3. Follow-up in three months for routine laboratory work and review of glucose trends.
explanations: No complication is documented: type 2 diabetes without complications.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Nothing in the note documents hyperglycemia or poor control.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
